**Finding submitted: `missing` (critical) — no liability cap in the Agreement.**

**What I found**
- Section 7 ("Limitation of Liability", p0026–p0027) consists of a single subsection: a mutual exclusion of consequential, incidental, indirect, punitive and special damages, expressly carved out for indemnification and confidentiality liability.
- Searches for "aggregate", "exceed" and liability language across the full body returned no monetary cap — none hidden in the warranty section (Section 9), indemnities (Sections 10–11) or termination/survival (p0070).
- Result: both parties bear **unlimited direct liability**. This fails the rule even though it is nominally mutual, and leaves AP exposed on the broad Customer indemnity in p0052 (Content, Properties, third-party acts).

**Drafting judgment on the cap basis**
Section 5 (p0023) is a **revenue share**, not a fee-paying arrangement — Customer pays Kubient nothing, and money flows from Kubient to AP. A standard "fees paid by Customer" cap would therefore be illusory (effectively zero) and would wipe out Kubient's liability to us. I used "amounts paid or payable between the Parties" with the USD 1,000,000 floor so the cap has real content in both directions.

**Redline inserted as new Section 7(b)** (validated `ok:true`):
- Mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000;
- Uncapped "Excluded Claims": confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP;
- Section 5 payment obligations expressly not treated as capped damages — important here, since Kubient owes AP the revenue share and should not be able to shelter unpaid amounts under the cap.

The comment states the playbook position, notes indemnities and confidentiality sit outside the cap, and offers the fallback (12 months' amounts with the four core carve-outs).
